engagement_title: FOLD & GRAIN Studio productizes the one take service: two live client runs, two takes, two shot boards that must not look alike, two sizzles with their platform set, two recovered client marks, and the recipe an assistant can run without us
vertical: Retail and e-commerce product photography, a three person studio in Portland, Oregon converting a day rate practice into a fixed price productized service, proven on a value pantry packaging line and a direct to consumer sterling silver capsule
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post from a small packaging design studio launching a new website, asking for an 'eye-catching sizzle reel to be used as the hero video on my new site' that is 'fast paced and energetic while showcasing my design work in the best way possible', to be built from 'mockups and photographs of packaging projects I have completed'. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com post from a growing direct to consumer sterling silver jewellery brand wanting a freelance editor to 'repurpose existing content into multiple formats and variations' for short form and social. Both posts are laundered: the studio becomes the coined FOLD & GRAIN Studio, its two client runs become the coined Cobbleway Provisions and Lunara Silver, and the ledger's non Western founder persona is replaced by Elodie Marchand. The STRENGTHEN verdict applies because the killed original sat almost entirely on one surface (reframe a clip, ship it) and because the ledger's own repositioning note concedes the original reframed an already vertical clip to vertical, a no operation that would also have enlarged. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is: HTML authoring now yields a native editable document at mixed canvas sizes, an ink level trace off photographed printed collateral recovers a real mark, and the video family shortens and reframes but never enlarges. So this is the commission both clients genuinely needed, which is not a reel but a repeatable service proven twice at two different price bands.
client_one_liner: We have sold days for six years and we want to sell a product instead: one continuous take per client and everything a small brand needs out of it, and these two runs are the proof, so if both clients come back looking like the same house look we have proved nothing.
client_brief:
FOLD & GRAIN Studio, service build

We are a three person product photography studio in Portland. For six years we have sold days. We want to sell a product instead: one continuous take per client, and out of that one take everything a small brand needs to sell the thing. Fixed price, fixed turnaround, no reshoot.

This engagement is the build and the proof. Two real client runs, both already shot, both from a single take with a grey card held in frame at the head.

Cobbleway Provisions is six matte kraft cartons, pantry goods, around eight dollars each, sold on their own web store and through two grocery co-ops. Lunara Silver is nine sterling pendants for Elodie Marchand, around a hundred and eighty dollars each, sold direct.

What each client gets. A shot board: every product in the range on one page, all of them looking like one afternoon rather than nine afternoons, with the piece name and the price under each. A short sizzle for the top of their site, plus a square one and a tall one for the places they post. And their own mark back as artwork, because neither of them still has the file. Cobbleway has a photograph of a printed carton. Lunara has a macro of the maker's stamp punched into a bail.

What we get is the recipe: written so our assistant can run it next Tuesday on a client we have not met, with the parameters, the order, and every place it can go wrong.

The two clients must not look alike. Cobbleway should read bright, honest, a little generous, the kind of thing you pick up without thinking. Lunara should read quiet and expensive: dark ground, restrained, the silver doing the work.

Nina's spoken walk through the range is on the end of the Cobbleway take, if it is usable.
price_band_and_audience: One engagement, two deliberately opposed client bands, plus the studio's own band. Cobbleway Provisions is pantry goods at roughly eight dollars a carton, bought off a shelf and off a small web store by a shopper aged twenty five to fifty five who decides in under two seconds: bright ground, generous product scale in the cell, warm honest colour, legible price, nothing precious. Lunara Silver is sterling pendants at roughly one hundred and eighty dollars, bought by a woman aged twenty eight to forty five who is buying restraint: dark stone ground, small product in a lot of air, cool restrained colour, no gloss, price set quietly. The band is load bearing twice over. Apply the bright generous treatment to the pendants and a one hundred and eighty dollar piece reads as costume, apply the restrained dark treatment to the cartons and eight dollar pantry goods read as unaffordable and stop selling. And because the whole pitch is a productized service, a single house look applied to both boards is not a stylistic slip, it is the proof failing: it demonstrates the studio cannot price tune, which is the one thing the service claims. FOLD & GRAIN itself bills around fifteen hundred dollars a day today and wants the product at a fixed twenty two hundred to three thousand five hundred dollars per client run. A posted job of this shape runs two thousand to four thousand five hundred dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: One take. Everything you need to sell it.
brand_identity.sector: Product photography studio moving from a day rate practice to a fixed price productized service
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2020 in Portland, Oregon. Three people: Nina (art direction and shooting), plus a retoucher and a studio assistant.
brand_identity.about: FOLD & GRAIN shoots small brands' products the way those brands actually sell them, in a row, as a range, rather than one hero at a time. For six years we sold days. We are now selling a product: one continuous take per client and, out of that single take, the shot board, the short films and the platform cuts a small brand needs to launch. Our work sits behind pantry goods at eight dollars and sterling silver at a hundred and eighty, and the whole point is that the same method tunes to each. Precision, repeatability and honesty about what a shoot can and cannot yield are the studio's stock in trade.
brand_identity.audience: Small and independent product brands (pantry, personal care, jewellery, homeware) launching or refreshing a web store and needing a full range shot to look like one afternoon. Founders who buy a fixed price and a fixed turnaround, not a day rate.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Repositioning from roughly fifteen hundred dollars a day to a fixed twenty two hundred to thirty five hundred dollars per client run. Mid-market, productized, premium to a freelancer but well under an agency.
brand_identity.typography: A clean neo-grotesque for headings and the studio wordmark, paired with a monospaced face for technical specs, parameters and captions on the service page. Type is set tight, quiet and utilitarian.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, specific, no salesmanship. We name what a shoot can deliver and what it cannot, and we write our recipes so an assistant could run them. Sentences are short and concrete.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: FOLD & GRAIN has a consistent working look built up over six years but never a codified system. There is a set wordmark and studio colours in practice, no written guidelines. This engagement, which includes the studio's own service page, is where the identity gets formalized for the first time.
brand_identity.values: Repeatability over one-off flourish, honesty about limits, and price-appropriate craft: a treatment right for one band is wrong for another, and saying so is the service.

assets_supplied.name: cobbleway_take_4k.mov (single continuous take, 3840 x 2160, about eleven minutes)
assets_supplied.kind: One unbroken slider pass across six matte kraft cartons on a pale seamless, grey card held in frame at the head, with the art director's spoken walk through the range recorded on the camera microphone during the final pass.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One take. Everything is in there, the card at the top and Nina's walk through at the end."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The last two and a half minutes are a lens capped reload with the walk through still running, and nothing in the file marks where that begins, so a machine chosen shortening has no reason to skip it and will happily spend seconds of a short sizzle on black. The microphone also sat across the room on the camera rather than on the speaker, so the walk through arrives carrying the room's slap and the slider's rumble rather than a usable voice.

assets_supplied.name: cobbleway_grabs/ (24 frame exports, 3840 x 2160, four per carton)
assets_supplied.kind: The assistant's on set frame exports pulled off that take, four per carton, straight out of the camera with nothing applied.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Four grabs per carton, straight off the take, nothing done to them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The window went behind cloud partway through the take and the operator re balanced the camera without saying so, so roughly half the grabs sit cooler than the rest, and the split is invisible on any single frame and only appears once six cartons are laid in a row. Two of the six cartons have grabs only from the cooler half, so bringing those two to the warmer family is a different move from correcting the other four.

assets_supplied.name: lunara_take_4k.mov (single continuous take, 2160 x 3840)
assets_supplied.kind: The pendant capsule take, nine sterling pieces on a dark stone slab under a strip softbox, grey card at the head, shot with the camera turned because the founder wanted the tall cut.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Same method, the silver capsule. Slower pass, the card is at the top."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The camera being turned means the take is taller than it is wide, so the wide site hero the studio's own spec calls for at two thousand five hundred and sixty across cannot be reached from it by any reframe that does not enlarge, and the reframe tool will not enlarge. The strip softbox also sits square on to several pieces, putting their brightest faces past recoverable and into flat paper white, which no preview distinguishes from merely bright.

assets_supplied.name: lunara_grabs/ (27 frame exports, three per piece)
assets_supplied.kind: Three frame exports per pendant off the same take, each piece caught at a slightly different point in the slider crawl.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Three grabs per piece, take your pick."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Which of a piece's three grabs sits under the clip is a property of how that individual piece happened to be lying on the slab, so the usable index is different for every one of the nine and cannot be predicted from the file order. Two of the nine pieces have no usable grab at all, which no filename, no folder and no preview reveals.

assets_supplied.name: client_marks/ (two photographs: cobbleway_carton_face.jpg, lunara_bail_stamp.jpg)
assets_supplied.kind: The only surviving evidence of each client's mark. One is a printed wordmark in a single deep ink on kraft board, photographed flat on a bench. The other is a macro of the maker's stamp punched into the bail of a pendant.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Neither of them has the file any more. This is all that is left."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They look like the same job and they are not: the printed one is ink on a substrate and traces, while the punched one carries no ink at all and exists only as the shadow inside a deformation in polished metal, so the route that works on the first returns a plausible looking blob on the second. The printed wordmark is also set in small caps with a hairline bracket on the serifs, which survives at canvas size and does not survive at the size the mark actually reproduces in a board caption strip.

assets_supplied.name: foldgrain_service_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the studio's own service description and turnaround, both clients' product names and prices as they must appear, and the caption copy for each board cell.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The words as they go out. Prices are current and cannot be edited."

acceptance_bar: Each shot board reads as ONE afternoon: one white point, one black point, one product scale in the cell and one crop logic across every product in that client's range. A range that is nearly consistent is not consistent.

The two boards must NOT read as the same look. Cobbleway bright, generous and warm at an eight dollar band, Lunara restrained, cool and dark at a one hundred and eighty dollar band. One house look applied to both fails the engagement even if both boards are individually good.

No delivered file exceeds the pixel or frame dimensions of the source it derives from, and no resize, crop or reframe in the run reports an enlargement. A deliverable that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even when it looks acceptable.
Every photograph is actually present and visible in the exported document on BOTH boards and on the service page, not only on the one an automatic preview happens to show.
Every product in each range has a frame that is genuinely usable, or is named in the note as not deliverable from this take. A cell is not filled by shipping the least bad grab.

Both client marks come back as placeable artwork rather than pictures of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and each still reads as that client's mark at the size it actually reproduces on its own board's ground.
On the boards the marks are live vector shapes and the captions and prices are text the client can retype, not a picture of a layout.
Both boards and the service page live in ONE working document, each keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
The sizzles are genuinely shorter than their takes and contain no dead footage, and the walk through either carries as usable voice or the sizzle ships without it and the note says which and why.
The platform set exists for each client at the sizes the brief names, or the shortfall is named with the reason, and no format in the set was reached by enlargement.
One type system across both boards and the service page, with the family, the foundry or designer, and the actual numeric weight recorded per role.
The recipe is runnable by someone who was not on this job: order, parameters applied per client, every place the pipeline can silently go wrong, and every limit the takes themselves impose.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked, including the light and dark portion and highlight controls), image_apply_preset, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every still decision in both client runs. It triages fifty one frame exports into their true colour families, fixes ONE target per client (two opposed targets, not one house look), corrects each frame toward its own client's target one call at a time, works out which pendant grabs carry recoverable highlight and which are already flat white, cuts every board frame to the cell aspect the board needs, and recovers two marks off two photographs that look like the same job and are not.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: Both shot boards and the studio's own service page as one native editable document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, which is the only surface in this connector that does free form fixed canvas layout. Every photograph must arrive as embedded image data by the route the importer actually keeps, the marks go in as inline SVG inside explicitly sized wrappers so they stay vector, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the payload travels by uploaded URL because a board of embedded photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

The motion half and the headline deliverable class. Metadata settles what each take physically is (including the turned camera on the pendant take), the summary settles where the content actually sits inside eleven minutes of continuous footage, speech enhancement decides whether a walk through recorded across a room can carry a sizzle, the quick cut shortens (and only shortens) each take into its hero, and the reframe produces the platform set without ever enlarging, which is what makes the wide pendant hero a decision rather than a click.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (called once per typographic role, never asked to pair), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system that has to serve two opposed price bands and the studio's own service page. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to hold a caption strip that reads honest at eight dollars and restrained at one hundred and eighty. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the entire kit, and the CSS must carry the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, orientation never passed), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the studio does not own, an in use bench atmosphere band for its own service page, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative candidates excluded and the licensed frame brought into the studio's own look rather than dropped in raw. The Boards half persists the two per client selects sets the clients sign off from, placed within the per call placement cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which of the six deliverable strands lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The boards and the service page need an authored fixed canvas document because the clients edit them and nothing else here composes free form layout; the sizzles and the platform set are video work; the marks are raster to vector recovery. The brief already pins every destination, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable strand, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload both takes, all fifty one frame exports, both mark photographs and the copy sheet through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, but at this count a manifest keyed by client and by product is the only thing that keeps a Lunara grab from being graded to the Cobbleway target sixty calls later.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by client, product and role.

trajectory.action: Read what each take physically is, then summarise both to learn where the content actually sits inside them.
trajectory.judgement: The pendant take was shot with the camera turned, which decides in advance what the wide site hero can and cannot be, and eleven minutes of continuous footage does not announce which minutes are worth anything. Both facts have to be known before any cut is attempted, not after.
trajectory.produces: Per take dimensions, duration and frame rate, plus a content map naming where the usable passes sit and where they do not.

trajectory.action: Preview all fifty one frame exports and triage them: which client, which product, which colour family each belongs to, and which pendant grabs carry a specular that is merely bright versus one that has gone flat.
trajectory.judgement: The studio asserts four grabs per carton and three per piece. The pictures are the only thing that can settle whether that is genuine coverage, and reading a row of six cartons together is a different act from looking at six frames one at a time, which is where the mid take rebalance actually becomes visible.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering client, product, apparent illuminant family, tilt, and a first read on highlight state.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop or cell decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop that was chosen against the unstraightened frame.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals left alone elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix ONE Cobbleway target off the best lit grab, bright, warm and honest at an eight dollar band, and bring all six cartons toward it with a separate call each, recording the parameters applied per carton.
trajectory.judgement: The destination is a set, not six good pictures. A single batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames that straddle a mid take rebalance, so the two cooler cartons reach the same destination by a different route from the four warmer ones.
trajectory.produces: Six Cobbleway masters at source scale with a per carton parameter log and a note on which family each came from.

trajectory.action: Apply confined corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong on kraft, selecting the material by its own visual properties rather than by the object it is printed on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the carton pulls the selection to the carton, naming the uncoated board's own colour and surface pulls it to the material. Warming the frame far enough to unify the two families takes the pale seamless with it unless the correction is confined.
trajectory.produces: Corrected Cobbleway frames where a global move would have taken the seamless muddy or the kraft orange.

trajectory.action: Fix a SEPARATE Lunara target, cool, restrained and dark at a one hundred and eighty dollar band, and bring the nine pendants toward it one call at a time, working the bright faces of the metal down into the frame.
trajectory.judgement: This target must not be the Cobbleway target with the numbers moved. The pendant band wants the silver holding shape against a dark slab rather than sparkling, so the move is a restraint move, and the pieces whose brightest faces will not come down are the ones the whole capsule turns on.
trajectory.produces: Nine Lunara masters at source scale, a per piece parameter log, and a first list of pieces that did not respond.

trajectory.action: Cut every board frame to the cell shape each board needs, product at one scale within the cell, reading the returned tradeoff record on every crop rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: Product scale within the cell is a band decision, generous for pantry goods and small in a lot of air for the pendants, and the tradeoff record is the only channel that reports what a crop actually did to a frame's dimensions.
trajectory.produces: Six Cobbleway cell frames and nine Lunara cell frames at their board aspects, each with its tradeoff record captured.

trajectory.action: Recover both client marks: triage the two photographs, select at ink or at deformation level by the mark's own visual properties, get polarity right, crop from the selection's own returned bounds, trace, then inject a viewBox and strip the opaque full canvas ground path.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word each selection so it takes the mark and not the substrate, which polarity to trace, and whether the same route can serve a punched metal stamp that carries no ink at all. Background removal is the wrong instrument on either of them.
trajectory.produces: Two placeable, scalable, transparent marks plus a note on which route each needed and why.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the bench atmosphere band the studio's own service page needs, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it into the studio's own look.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the studio's page rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded to the service page.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: One system has to hold two opposed bands. The pairing is the agent's own art direction, the weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one bad name in the kit call kills every good one with it.
trajectory.produces: A single kit type system with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, the Cobbleway board, the Lunara board and the studio service page, with every board frame embedded as image data, each mark placed as inline SVG in an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper at the size it actually reproduces in the caption strip, family and weight declared on every text element, and every root declaring its own canvas.
trajectory.judgement: An auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much air each band takes and how large each mark can sit above its captions.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying both boards and the service page, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, upload the file, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first board, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the second board and the service page.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard, so looking at board one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the other two.

trajectory.action: Put the walk through through speech enhancement and judge whether what comes back can carry a client's hero video.
trajectory.judgement: A microphone across the room in a hard room is a different problem from a noisy microphone, and enhancement is not a substitute for proximity. If it does not carry, the honest answer is a sizzle without voice and a line in the note, not a hero video with a voice nobody can follow.
trajectory.produces: An enhanced walk through and a written yes or no on whether it ships.

trajectory.action: Shorten each take into its hero sizzle and watch what the machine actually chose, against the content map made in step three.
trajectory.judgement: The cut tool shortens and picks its own beats; it does not know a lens cap from a carton. The content map is the only standard the result can be judged against, and a sizzle that opens on black is a delivered failure that reports success.
trajectory.produces: Two hero sizzles judged against the content map, with any dead footage named.

trajectory.action: Reframe each sizzle into its platform set at the sizes the brief names, never enlarging, and settle the wide pendant hero.
trajectory.judgement: The pendant take was shot turned, so its wide hero cannot reach the studio's stated site width from these pixels by any honest route. The choice is to deliver it at the width the take supports and say so, or to build that one hero on the authored canvas surface instead, and either is defensible only if it is stated.
trajectory.produces: A platform set per client with no enlargement anywhere, plus a written decision on the wide pendant hero.

trajectory.action: Create a selects board per client and add the graded set within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed.
trajectory.judgement: A two hundred and one is partial success rather than an error, and the recovered marks are not boardable, so they belong in the note instead of being pushed at a surface that will not take them.
trajectory.produces: Two persistent shareable boards with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Write the service pack: the recipe in running order, the parameters applied per client, every place the pipeline silently goes wrong, and every limit these two takes imposed on what could be delivered.
trajectory.judgement: The recipe is the actual product being built, so it has to be specific enough that an assistant who was not here can run it on a client nobody has met, and honest enough to name what this method cannot do.
trajectory.produces: The repeatable pipeline recipe, the per client parameter log, and the named limitations.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the bright faces of the sterling pieces are merely bright or are already gone. The strip softbox sat square on to several pieces, and on those the brightest faces are clipped flat rather than steeply lit. A recovery move on a clipped face succeeds, returns a file, and changes nothing at all: there is no warning, no flag and no numeric readout anywhere in the response, and the only signal is that the before and the after look identical when put beside each other. Which pieces are affected is a property of how each individual piece happened to be lying on the slab, and two of the nine have no usable grab among their three at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering dodges it and no parameter prevents it, because merely bright and already flat look the same in a preview and differ only in what a recovery move can do to them. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the strip light was used and that the pendants should read restrained, which is art direction rather than a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different route entirely, working back through the other grabs of that piece to find the index that sits under the clip, and where none does, accepting that the piece cannot be delivered from this take and saying so.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compare each Lunara result against its input rather than reading the response, and for every piece where nothing moved go back to that piece's other grabs, re grade the replacement toward the same restrained target, and re cut its board cell, since a different grab is a different angle and therefore a different crop. For the pieces with no usable grab, name them in the note rather than filling the cell.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A nine piece capsule board for a one hundred and eighty dollar direct to consumer brand in which several pendants carry a flat white hole where the metal should have shape, on the one deliverable whose whole argument is that restraint reads expensive.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each recovered mark survives at the size it actually reproduces on its own board's ground. Both traces look correct at canvas size. The Cobbleway wordmark is set in small caps with a hairline bracket on the serifs, and the tracer takes no options at all, so the only lever on its output is the raster it was fed. At the size the mark sits in a caption strip, on the deep ink panel the restrained board uses, the counters of the small letters close up and the hairline goes, and what remains reads as a dark lozenge rather than as that client's name. None of this is visible at full canvas, and the trace reports success either way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) It cannot be ordered around: the mark has to exist before it can be placed, and it has to be placed at real size on the real ground before anyone can see what it becomes there. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for the mark back as artwork and the acceptance bar carries the client's standing requirement that it still read as their mark, which is a requirement rather than a warning that a trace closes counters. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the answer is a different asset produced by a different route, either the colour accurate knockout plate traced instead of the two colour route, or a coarser raster prep that keeps the counters open, and where neither holds, a larger mark and a re architected caption strip built around it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare the raster the trace is fed, re trace, re inject the viewBox and re strip the ground path, then re place at reproduction size on the actual panel colour and look again rather than at the tool's response. Where the mark still will not hold, redesign the caption strip around a mark that can, which changes the board's cell proportions and forces the cell frames cut in step nine to be recut.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Two clients' marks handed back as artwork that is legible only at a size neither of them will ever use, on a service whose written promise is that the client gets their mark back.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the way the board's photograph cells were built. A contact sheet cell wants a photograph that fills a fixed rectangle and crops to it, which the natural authoring route gives for free by setting the photograph as the cell's background rather than as a placed element. The importer keeps the cell, keeps its geometry, keeps its border and keeps its caption, and discards the photograph entirely, returning an empty box in exactly the right place. The response is a success with no warning of any kind, the structure of the board looks right, and the document's own preview shows the first artboard only, so the second board and the service page can be checked through no channel except the returned markup.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Doing it right the first time requires knowing which of two equally reasonable constructions the importer keeps, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates, and the readiness pass raises nothing. Ordering cannot help because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last act. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for boards the client can edit and the acceptance bar asks that the photographs actually be present on both boards, which is the client's requirement rather than a disclosure about a construct. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the surviving construction is a placed element with explicit dimensions, which does not crop to its box, so every cell frame has to be pre cut to the cell aspect upstream in the imaging surface before the board can be re authored at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the imaging surface three steps back, re cut all fifteen board frames to their exact cell aspects, re author both boards around placed elements in explicitly sized wrappers, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and then audit all three canvases from the returned markup rather than from the one artboard the preview offers.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Two shot boards delivered as an editable document in which the cartons and the pendants are absent and every caption, price and rule is perfectly in place, with the export having reported success at every step and the only artboard anyone looked at being the one that happened to work.

decision_gates: Which strands are still work, which are motion work, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout and only one produces motion.
Whether four grabs per carton and three per piece is genuine coverage, which the file counts assert and only the pictures can settle.
Whether the six cartons are one shoot. The studio believes they nearly are; a row of six is the only place that can be answered.
How far to push the two cartons that exist only in the cooler family before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.
Two targets or one. The commercial argument of the whole engagement is that the same method price tunes, so a single house look is the correct looking wrong answer.
Product scale within the cell, which is a band decision: generous for pantry goods, small in a lot of air for pendants, and swapping them misprices both clients.
Which grab of each pendant carries recoverable highlight, and what to do about the pieces where none does.

Selection wording on each mark photograph: naming the substrate takes the carton, naming the ink's own visual properties takes the wordmark, and a punched stamp carrying no ink at all is not the same problem wearing a different hat.
Which mark route survives at reproduction size, judged on the actual ground colour rather than at full canvas.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, holding two opposed bands and a service page on one system, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Whether the walk through recorded across a room can carry a client's hero video after enhancement, or whether the honest deliverable is a sizzle without voice.

What to do about the wide pendant hero, given a turned take that cannot reach the stated site width without enlargement: deliver narrower and say so, or build that hero on the authored canvas surface instead.
Whether a machine chosen shortening actually landed on the range or on the reload, judged against the content map rather than against the response.
How much of the recipe is the parameters and how much is the failure modes, since the parameters are what an assistant can copy and the failure modes are what the service is actually selling.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns attractive pictures of kraft cartons and silver pendants. IDENTITY: these are two specific clients' actual products with their actual prices, and each client's mark must be RECOVERED off the only photograph that survives rather than reinvented, because a regenerated wordmark is a different company's logo and a regenerated stamp is not the maker's mark at all. SPEC: the boards are fixed canvases carrying exact caption copy and current prices that cannot be edited, the platform set has named sizes that must be reached without a single enlarged pixel from takes whose dimensions cap what is reachable, and the sizzles must be genuinely derived from the clients' own continuous takes rather than assembled from anything else. EDITABILITY: the boards and the service page are defined by being editable, since prices move, pieces sell out and the studio's own service copy is still being written, and the whole product being built is a recipe another person runs, which is a document rather than a picture. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality that no generator participates in: did this highlight recovery change anything at all, does this trace still read as the client's name at eight millimetres on a deep ground, did the photographs actually arrive in the document or only their empty boxes, and did the machine's cut land on the range or on the lens cap.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor, fill_area, remove_background and vectorize are all verified headless across twenty seven live calls. VECTOR RECOVERY: the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry (the same tool returned a card shaped blob for one wording and a stroke only ink mask for another), the mask polarity trap before tracing, the tracer taking no options at all so the raster prep is the only lever, the missing viewBox and the opaque path at index zero are all live findings, and the acceptance bar scores exactly the hygiene the tool does not perform. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, real tables and per cell strokes survive, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, CSS background images are documented as DROPPED ENTIRELY while the element keeps its geometry, and the rendition preview is documented as FIRST ARTBOARD ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup and why the third checkpoint is real. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because fifteen embedded board frames pass the seventy kilobyte inline threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load, with the all or nothing kit call and the non standard numeric weights as live traps. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real seven thousand three hundred and sixty by four thousand nine hundred and twelve JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of twelve placements per call and a two hundred and one meaning partial. VIDEO AND AUDIO: the task uses only the Premiere set sanctioned for authoring here, video_metadata to read what each take is, media_summarize, media_enhance_speech, video_create_quick_cut which only shortens and chooses its own beats, and video_resize which never enlarges, and the turned pendant take is a genuine dimensional constraint rather than an assumed one. Deliberately, NO graded checkpoint rests on a video artefact: all three rest on the imaging and Express surfaces that are verified synchronous and retrievable, so the task remains gradeable in full. AVOIDED: no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no generative fill or expand, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no variable QR, no batch above twenty.
